headline.caveat: OpenAI-designed custom accelerators + Broadcom Ethernet networking, deploying 2H2026 through end-2029; contract dollars undisclosed (a known data gap)

realized_to_date.caveat: rack deployments targeted to start 2H2026; nothing quantified publicly

nature_md: Announced Oct 13, 2025: OpenAI designs its own AI accelerators and systems (embedding frontier-model learnings into silicon), Broadcom co-develops and deploys them — 10GW of racks scaled entirely with Broadcom Ethernet, across OpenAI facilities and partner data centers, starting 2H2026 and completing by end-2029. This is OpenAI's hedge against NVIDIA/AMD pricing and its bid for Google-style TPU economics. No contract value has ever been disclosed; Broadcom's FY26 AI revenue guidance (~$56B) and its reported ~$10B 'fourth custom ASIC customer' backlog entry (widely believed to be OpenAI) are the only public financial traces.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Undisclosed purchase commitments; custom-silicon programs typically involve NRE payments during development plus per-unit purchases on delivery — none of it visible in public filings since OpenAI is private.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Broadcom books custom-accelerator (XPU) and networking revenue on shipment within its AI semiconductor segment; analysts track OpenAI as one of a small set of custom-ASIC customers (with Google, Meta, and now Anthropic-linked TPU volumes) — deep customer concentration in the segment.

events.title: OpenAI and Broadcom announce 10GW custom-accelerator collaboration
